title: Private smokecheck auto-fix + safe rollback for Terraform-managed VPC nodes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a deterministic, auditable auto-fix flow for transient Private (VPC) "health check" failures detected by the smokecheck service, while preserving safe rollback and human-in-the-loop escalation. This ticket implements runbook v2: an automated remediation orchestrator that executes targeted Terraform repairs, lightweight node recreation, and KV cache warmup, plus a staged rollback if remediation worsens user-visible signals.

Background: We see recurring Class B incidents where the smokecheck pipeline reports 2–5 node-level probe failures after upgrades or cloud provider maintenance. Current manual remediation is error-prone (ad-hoc terraform apply, node restarts). This work codifies the fix-playbook into an automated workflow with clear bailouts and audit trail.

Goals:
- Detect actionable failures with conservative thresholds (e.g., private_probe_failure_count > 4 in 10m AND vpc.node_heartbeat_missing > 3m).
- Run safe targeted repairs: terraform plan --target=module.private_nodes.aws_instance.vpc_node[INDEX] and only apply if plan json diffs are limited to known drift patterns.
- Provide an automated alternative path that performs a controlled node recreate (cordon+drain -> create replacement -> attach -> warm KV cache).
- If remediation increases failure rate (>10% regression in 15m), automatically rollback to prior Terraform lockfile/AMI and notify SRE/PM.
- Keep operator in loop with Slack/PagerDuty notifications and a single-click UI action in Console to approve or abort automated fixes.

Runbook snippets and thresholds (operator-facing):
1) Trigger detection: Alert if metric private.vpc.smokecheck_failure_count > 4 (10m window) OR grafana panel "Private Smokecheck" shows sustained red for 2 consecutive polls.
2) Pre-checks (automated): verify terraform workspace matches cluster (terraform workspace list | grep ${cluster}), ensure state lock acquired (terraform force-unlock if stale lock_count < 2), snapshot current state (terraform state pull > state-snapshot.json).
3) Target selection: pick nodes with probe_failures > 3 and heartbeat_missing > 180s. Limit to 1 node per remediation cycle for canary.
4) Terraform dry-run: terraform plan -out=plan.bin -target=module.private_nodes.aws_instance.vpc_node[IDX] && terraform show -json plan.bin > plan.json. Reject if plan.json contains more than 10 resource diffs or any replacements in core networking resources.
5) Apply: terraform apply -auto-approve plan.bin (run inside ephemeral CI runner with role assumption).
6) Post-apply verification: smokecheck run (python tools/smokecheck/run.py --target node-${id}) with expected pass rate >= 90% over 5 minutes. If pass, promote (next node can be remediated).
7) KV warmup: run kv-cache-warmup job (kubectl -n private run kv-warmup --image=redwood/kv-warmup:stable --env TARGET=node-${id}) to reduce first-token latency and avoid regressions.
8) Rollback criteria: if error_rate increases by 10% or more in 15 minutes OR more than 2 dependent services show degrading SLOs, trigger rollback. Rollback steps: a) snapshot current deployment (git tag infra/rollback/ENG-83001/${timestamp}), b) terraform apply using last-known-good plan file (artifact store path), c) if terraform rollback fails, fall back to AMI swap and node-level recreate, d) escalate to on-call ENG lead.

Operator commands (copy-paste friendly):
- Check current alerts: curl -sS https://api.alerts.redwood.ai/v1/alerts?filter=private_smokecheck | jq .
- Grab plan for node 2: terraform plan -target=module.private_nodes.aws_instance.vpc_node[2] -out=plan.bin && terraform show -json plan.bin > plan.json && jq '.resource_changes|length' plan.json
- Force-lock state if needed: terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID || echo "no stale lock"
- Run smokecheck locally: python tools/smokecheck/run.py --node node-2 --timeout 300

Automation design (high level):
- A serverless orchestrator service (remediator) subscribes to smokecheck alerts. It runs the pre-checks, generates the targeted terraform plan, uploads the plan artifact to the infra artifacts bucket, and posts a Slack message with an approval button.
- When 'Auto-approve' is enabled for low-risk clusters, the remediator proceeds and triggers a ephemeral CI runner job to apply the plan under least-privilege role.
- All state-modifying actions are recorded as immutable artifacts (plan.json, state-snapshot.json, smokecheck-results.json) and linked in the Slack thread for audit.
- Metric checks run via embedded Grafana synthetic queries. Rollback jobs are implemented as separate ephemeral CI jobs that restore the last-known-good plan.

Safety and guardrails:
- Limit remediation to 1 node per 30 minutes per cluster by default.
- Require approval for clusters tagged 'prod' unless incident meets P0 criteria.
- Never touch core networking (VPC, subnets, routing) via auto-apply; terraform plan must not include aws_vpc/aws_subnet replacements when run by remediator.
- Always snapshot and upload state to S3 with a checksum.

Audit & Postmortem:
- The remediator writes a remediation-event entry to /events/remediations with fields: cluster, node, plan_sha, operator, outcome. This file is immutable and used by the postmortem tooling.
- Postmortem template: collect artifact links, smokecheck timeline, terraform plan diffs, and regression metric graphs.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (week 1): alert tuning + pre-check scripts + plan artifact pipeline.
- M2 (week 2): remediator MVP that posts Slack approvals and can execute dry-run plans.
- M3 (week 3): automatic apply with canary limit and KV warmup hook.
- M4 (week 4): rollback automation + audit trail + SRE runbook integration.

Notes / Caveats:
- Some cloud providers return instance metadata drift for benign reasons; the plan rejection heuristic must be conservative to avoid unnecessary node replacement.
- AMI rollbacks depend on AMI lifecycle guarantees from infra-team; coordinate with images team for fallback images.

Deliverables:
- Full runbook page (Confluence) with one-click Console button spec.
- Remediator service PR with unit + integration tests.
- Terraform plan artifacts stored in infra-artifacts S3 with encryption.
- SRE training doc + runbook whitelabel for customers running Private with 'self-managed' tag.
steps: Tune alert thresholds and create test alert channel
Implement pre-check and plan generation scripts
Build remediator MVP that posts Slack approvals
Wire ephemeral CI job to apply targeted plans
Add KV warmup and smokecheck verification hooks
Implement rollback automation and audit artifacts
Run chaos tests in staging and validate safety gates
remediation_playbook: Phase 0: Silence noisy alerts and gather snapshots
Phase 1: Run targeted plan dry-run and evaluate diffs
Phase 2: Apply canary fix to single node and validate
Phase 3: Warmup KV cache and monitor 15m
Phase 4: Promote or rollback depending on metrics
Phase 5: Close incident and attach artifacts to postmortem
